analysis.title: 10/28 Mkt Internal Insight: FOMC Non-Event; RM Support; Buy Flow/Outperf in AI & High SI
key_insights: Excess buy flow of +$15bn and retail buy-the-dip at the 66th percentile vs 3Y persisted despite SPX -1% and QQQ -2%.
The morning QQQ drawdown (around 10-11am) was triggered by CTAs. Two NQ1 sell triggers crossed, at pre-open and at 10:27am.
Further systematic selling is possible today and tomorrow. Leveraged ETPs are estimated to sell $22bn, mostly in QQQ and tech. ES1 has 6 sell triggers and NQ1 has 3 sell triggers within -2%.
Risk control selling becomes meaningful only if SPX falls 2% today. At the current -1.04%, estimated rebalancing is $20-30bn to sell, about $5-10bn today and $15-20bn tomorrow.

Internals look better than last Friday: no sign of a risk parity unwind, equity/bond correlation is negative again, VIX cross-asset rank is 43%, VIX/SPX hi-low ratio is 2.3x vs 4.1x on Friday, and SPX dealer gamma is nearly flat.
UBS expects the current systematic selling to be violent but short-lived, a day or two, depending on how much risk control has to sell.
The 1M equity/bond price correlation is -20%, the first negative reading since March. UBS reads this as Treasuries working again as a flight-to-safety asset, which helps multi-asset diversification.
The buy tilt continues in ETFs and tech (semis and hardware). Nasdaq excess sell flow was only -$16bn against a -2.1% QQQ move.
Leveraged ETP AUM fell to $139bn (58th percentile vs 5Y), so rebalance sensitivity is now $7.2bn per 1% underlying move.
Estimated leveraged ETP rebalance is $21.7bn to sell, of which $20.1bn is in NDX and tech: $11.1bn semis, $6.1bn QQQ, $746mn MAG-7, $2.1bn rest of tech.

sector_views.rationale: Retail and institutional buy flow continues in semis and hardware, while leveraged ETP rebalancing puts the heaviest forced selling in semis, with several names above 20% of ADV.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The FOMC was not a market driver. The move in equities was attributed to CTA-triggered selling.
First negative correlation since March. Treasuries are acting as a risk-off hedge again.

risk_factors: Further CTA selling, with 6 ES1 and 3 NQ1 sell triggers within -2%.
Leveraged ETP selling of about $22bn, concentrated in QQQ and tech.
Risk control selling would become meaningful if SPX falls 2% or more, with $135-180bn to sell in total.
Semis face concentrated forced selling, with several names above 20% of ADV.
vol_and_positioning: VIX is 18.8 with a cross-asset rank of 43%, described as benign.
VIX/SPX intraday hi-low ratio is 2.3x, versus 4.1x on Friday, when it signaled hedging anxiety not matched by equity moves.
SPX dealer gamma is flat. Between 7200 and 8200 the profile sits between -$8bn and +$5bn. Yesterday it turned long gamma at +$36bn around 2:50pm, against under +$5bn long at the open.
ES1 exposure is at the 71st percentile vs 3Y, NQ1 at the 32nd and RTY1 at the 10th.
NQ1 close sell triggers: 29035 (ST -1.0%), 28961 (LT -1.2%), 28896 (MT -1.4%). The next is about -2.7% away.
RTY1 has no close sell trigger and one close buy trigger at 2811.9 (ST +0.8%).

Risk control scenarios: SPX -1.5% means $65-85bn to sell ($20-30bn today, $40-55bn tomorrow). SPX -2% means $135-180bn ($45-60bn today, $90-120bn tomorrow). SPX -2.5% means $200-280bn ($60-80bn today, $140-200bn tomorrow).

The top semis to sell as a share of ADV in the leveraged ETP rebalance are NXPI (50.8%), ADI (43.5%), MPWR (41.8%), MCHP (35.0%), TXN (34.2%), TER (33.3%), QCOM (26.1%), KLAC (26.1%), ON (20.8%) and AEM (19.9%).
The top stocks to sell in dollars are NVDA, MU, AMD, AVGO, INTC, AAPL, MSFT, MRVL, TXN and ADI.
